big: Rohan, a resident in Mumbai, wants to buy US shares. He cannot simply wire money. He must use a bank that handles foreign exchange, state his purpose, and respect a yearly limit under a scheme called LRS.

h: Sending money out as a resident
lines: Can I send money abroad to invest?
Yes, under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme. There is a yearly limit per person, the purpose must be permitted, and the bank may collect tax at source. Education only, not advice.

rows: Lets a resident send up to a set amount abroad each year for permitted purposes
Investing, education, travel, gifts and similar
Tax collected at source by the bank, adjustable against your tax
A bank permitted by RBI to handle foreign exchange
note: The limit is USD 250,000 per person each financial year at the time of writing. Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.
